fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Walkway; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Open Lawn Area; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of approach.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back plants and shrubs growing against or directly adjacent to the main residence and detached structure.
• Thin dense vegetation between the front driveway and the structures so responders can move on foot without obstruction.
• Mark the rear of the property with a visible indicator showing whether a gate or opening exists for emergency access.
• If a rear gate exists in the perimeter fencing, keep it unlocked or install a Knox-style padlock so responders can access the rear without delay.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear of overgrown vegetation so responders can move between buildings quickly.
• Identify a flat, firm staging area on the open lawn that emergency vehicles or crews can use without entering dense vegetation.
• Post the property address on both the front and rear of the main residence so responders approaching from different directions can confirm the location.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Large Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Single Access Route; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches and shrubs that are directly touching or overhanging the roof and walls of the structure.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to create open gaps between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees close to the structure, cutting them up from the ground to at least 10 feet high.
• Clear shrubs and small plants growing directly against the foundation and walls of the structure.
• Separate shrubs and small trees growing beneath the large trees to reduce how easily fire could climb from the ground into the tree canopy.
• Thin scattered trees and mixed shrubs on the sides of the property where vegetation grows closest to the structure.
• Cut back and remove vegetation growing along both edges of the driveway to keep it passable and clear of overhanging branches.
• Maintain a mowed or cleared strip along the driveway so vehicles can move freely without vegetation crowding the travel surface.
• Keep the single driveway entrance clearly marked and free of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can enter without obstruction.
• Remove dead branches, dead shrubs, and accumulated dry plant material from beneath trees and around the structure.
• Thin mixed vegetation between tree clusters so open ground is visible between plant groupings near the structure.
